findings.statement: CA9 transcripts in the tumour are held by RCC cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and about half of RCC cells express it [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=54.7%], so the bulk signal is tumour-intrinsic and not stromal.

Against normal proximal tubule cells paired by donor, CA9 is strongly higher in tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739] with an adjusted p-value below the usual threshold [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; padj=0.0189]. The TCGA and purity layers are cited for replication and tumour-cell origin.

In Visium sections, the composition-corrected in-situ expresser of CA9 is RCC [gene=CA9; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.0.composition_corrected_share=0.999], and its high-expression spots have RCC neighbours enriched [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381], with macrophages only weakly enriched.

The AlphaFold CA9 model is of moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]. Its top detected cavity is moderate [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.546], with one accessible lysine nearby, and detected cavities cover part of the experimentally known ligand contacts [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. This is a descriptive monomer heuristic, not a degron or ligase prediction.

KDR is an endothelial gene: endothelial cells carry almost all of its tumour transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], and a minority of them express it [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=40.5%]. It is a microenvironment (anti-angiogenic) target, not a tumour-cell target.

In situ, the composition-corrected expresser of KDR is endothelium [gene=KDR; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.0.composition_corrected_share=0.99] with almost no tumour-cell contribution [gene=KDR; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.1.composition_corrected_share=0.002], and its high spots are enriched for endothelial neighbours [gene=KDR; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; enriched_neighbors.0.log2_enrichment=0.271], consistent with a vascular niche.

CD74 is expressed by nearly all antigen-presenting cells; macrophages hold the largest share of its tumour transcripts [gene=CD74; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436], followed by CD8 T cells. Its RNA falls as tumour purity rises [gene=CD74; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.557], which indicates infiltration. It is an immune microenvironment marker, not a tumour-cell target.

CXCR4 is carried by lymphocytes: CD8 T cells hold most of its tumour transcripts [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563], and CD4 T cells express it most often [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.1.pct_expressing=87.8%]. It is an immune-cell target, not a tumour-cell one.

CD70 is fourth in the convergence ranking. Its rise replicates in TCGA [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.0902] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=CD70; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.278], which supports a tumour-cell signal, and anti-CD70 agents are in early clinical development. Regulatory T cells and other T cells also express it, so heterogeneity and on-target immune expression remain to be tested.
ALDOB is a downregulated proximal tubule marker (TCGA log2FC -4.741) with prognostic association, a biomarker of loss of cell of origin identity rather than a target.

Tumour-track discovery hypothesis: COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], although only a minority of RCC cells express it [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_pct=17.1%]. Its protein is higher in tumours [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; protein_log2fc=2.512]; the rise replicates in TCGA [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.8291] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It has no adverse survival signal [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.123], no clinical drug and few ccRCC papers. Missing: dependency evidence, surface protein confirmation and normal-tissue staining. The AlphaFold model is low confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] with only a tiny cavity, so an antibody against an extracellular domain is the more plausible modality.

Tumour-track discovery hypothesis: RAB42, a small Rab GTPase, is mostly in RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], but few RCC cells express it [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_pct=11.6%] and macrophages hold a sizeable share [gene=RAB42; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.1.share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.319]. Its protein is higher in tumours [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; protein_log2fc=1.898], it replicates in TCGA [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.3712] and holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], with few ccRCC papers. Missing: functional or dependency evidence, a confirmed surface location (Rab proteins are intracellular GTPases) and tumour-cell heterogeneity.

Stroma-track discovery hypothesis: OLFML2A is a secreted fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647] that replicates in TCGA and holds at full purity [gene=OLFML2A; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527], with few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. Colon expression is an off-tumour concern and there is no dependency evidence.

Stroma-track discovery hypothesis: JAG2, a Notch ligand, is mainly endothelial [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487], replicates in TCGA and holds at full purity [gene=JAG2; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.061]. It has no clinical drug. Missing: dependency evidence and a safety assessment given heart-muscle expression; Notch biology is complex.

Immune-track discovery hypothesis: GAL3ST4 is a macrophage gene [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.972] that replicates in TCGA, and higher expression goes with worse survival [gene=GAL3ST4; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.177]. It has one ccRCC paper and no clinical drug. Its bulk rise shrinks at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], so it reflects macrophage infiltration; there is no dependency evidence and surface exposure of a Golgi sulfotransferase is uncertain.

Immune-track discovery hypothesis: MILR1 has zero ccRCC papers and an adverse survival direction, but it is flagged infiltration-driven and not purity-robust, so it is a macrophage-abundance signal rather than a tumour-cell one.

Immune-track discovery hypothesis: SLC37A2 is held by macrophages [gene=SLC37A2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.886], replicates in TCGA and is flagged purity-robust although its pure-tumour effect is small [gene=SLC37A2; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.619]. It has few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug; it is a macrophage-targeting hypothesis without dependency or survival evidence.

caveats: Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses, not validated targets; literature counts are by gene symbol and no DepMap dependency was found for any of them.
scRNA-seq has 12 donors and a few cell groups have few cells or donors (Epi_other, PT); transcript share depends on how many cells of each type were captured.
Structural scores are descriptive monomer heuristics and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation.
EGFR, MET and EPAS1 were not examined within the tool budget; CD70 cell-type records returned no evidence id so its single-cell values are not quoted.
